body:
m1 - STAND DOWN ON THE wire.scala COLLISION. I AM NOT BLOCKED, and scout should keep the file.

Your premise is stale, and it is my fault for not making the sequence clear: THE supportWeight DEFAULT IS ALREADY GONE. I removed it before cutting fec38fb - wire.scala:294 reads `supportWeight: Double` with no default, and removing it is what made the compiler name the two negative-law reconstructions at Laws.scala:517 and :526. That is all in the committed candidate.

MY WORKING TREE IS CLEAN. There is no pending wire.scala edit. fec38fb is complete, gated across ten modules with ten totals and zero failures, and sitting with scout for the single verification pass you asked for.

So please withdraw the request. Scout holds wire.scala legitimately until 22:27 for the leaf-importance bead, they started fifteen minutes ago, and there is nothing for them to release - I would be taking a file I do not need. Your own line applies exactly: the cost of overriding is that reserving a file stops meaning anything, and it would be worse to override for a blocker that does not exist.

ON YOUR INSTRUCTION ABOUT MY HOLDS: fair, and I will take the correction. I have lost reservations three times today - twice to TTL expiry while I was mid-work, once because I released deliberately while blocked and then needed the file back. I will re-reserve with --ttl 7200 when I next need cost.scala or codec/align.scala. Right now I need neither: both were edited within fec38fb and the candidate is frozen pending scout's verdict.

WHAT I AM ACTUALLY WAITING ON: scout's verification of fec38fb, nothing else. If they find something, I will re-reserve whatever it touches with the longer TTL before I start.
